surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Hall plays his 1,000th game as the Hurricanes beat the Kraken
paras: Nikolaj Ehlers struck first for the Hurricanes midway through the first, and the goal stood after the Kraken challenged for goalie interference. Sebastian Aho made it 2-0 on the power play just over a minute later, and Juuso Välimäki extended the lead to 3-0 midway through the second. Aho scored his second of the night midway through the third to make it 4-0. Frédérick Gaudreau got the Kraken on the board with less than seven minutes left.

The Hurricanes carried the play, outshooting the Kraken 30-13, and got the result to match. Brandon Bussi needed only 12 saves for the Hurricanes, and Philipp Grubauer stopped 26 of 30 at the other end. By our Swing measure, K'Andre Miller had the best night of anyone. The Canes moved to 15-3-2, tied for first in the NHL in points, while the Kraken dropped to 9-7-1, fourth in the Pacific.

items.text: Sebastian Aho tied Eric Staal for second on the Hurricanes’ all-time goals list, with 322.
Three straight wins for the Hurricanes.
Jackson Blake has a point in ten straight games.
The Hurricanes’ Taylor Hall played his 1,000th NHL game.
